utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I did not know of such breaches, nor was I personally informed about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you heard nothing about incidences that happened during the course of April of 1993 by HVO soldiers or allegedly committed by HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I must repeat. I did hear that there were persons that were interned at that institution and this is all I know. I don't know anything about any breaches.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, didn't it occur to you that it might be, even if you had no direct jurisdiction bestowed on you by some formal act of the prosecutor, didn't it occur to you to speak to the prosecutor or the minister of the justice or somebody else if you saw and knew this to be happening?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I did not see such things happening. I must say once again that I had no physical access to that prison at that time, so I couldn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about outside of the prison, did you receive reports of breaches of the Geneva conventions and other possible war crimes by commanders of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Such reports could only be submitted to the prosecutor's office, not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Whether it came through the prosecutor's office or directly, did Colonel Blaskic, for example, contact you and tell you about crimes that allegedly were being committed by his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about Dario Kordic, did he make contact with you? Mr. Aleksovski did, what about Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, I think you said in March that you went down to the prison in Kaonik and then I think you went later, was that, in what, July? Can you remember the next time when you went?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Which time frame do you have in mind, before the month of July or after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, you just tell me, if you might, and assist me as best you can, when did you go there during the course of 1993, to the Kaonik facility? You've mentioned going there in late '92, in January '93, in March, 1993, now you also said July I think?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go in April?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I went in April, it was a long time ago, but I remember these visits that took place after the conflict and after the communications were re-established. This is why I remember these particular visits. They all took place in 1993, especially in the second half of 1993 when it was possible to travel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now when you travelled down to the road from Travnik or from Vitez to the Kaonik facility, you would have seen destroyed buildings on the side of the road, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And did you know whether or not these buildings were Muslims' houses or Croat houses or were you able to distinguish?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I personally didn't make any distinction, I don't know that area very well. I was born in Travnik and I was raised there and Travnik is the largest town in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You drove past the Village of Ahmici, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Take a look at this photograph for me. If it could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 134.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now that's the Mosque at Ahmici, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And as you drive from Vitez down to Busovaca and particularly to Kaonik, this is set back off the road, but you can see it from the road, from the main highway?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to see. Actually, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But you saw this, didn't you, during 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You didn't at any stage see the mosque in Ahmici had been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I saw that the entire village was destroyed and I didn't make any distinction from between buildings, houses and the mosque because the mosque is, I think, situated some 100 metres away from the road. And I didn't stray from the road because of the danger. I was not a member of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So when did you first see this?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I personally never entered that village. I, again, have to stress that even after the truce, I never went to the village. I never went to the Municipality of Vitez before that. I never visited this particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you never received a report either during 1993 or subsequently relating to an investigation into the destruction of religious monuments by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I told you that such a report could only be submitted to the prosecutor's office and not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My question is you never saw such a report?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know an incident where a judge by the name of Judge Kemal was murdered?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I heard about that case, but I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it ever investigated so far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: This could only be investigated by the police. As far as I know, the perpetrator was never found.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And this occurred in April/May of 1993 in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: It didn't occur in Travnik, it occurred outside Travnik and I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember or did you ever receive a report about a bomb that was placed in a truck which exploded on or about the 18th of April, 1993, in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, with your permission the Defence would like to ask the colleague from the Prosecution what is the reason for these questions? Obviously they don't have anything to do with the Kaonik facility, which is the subject of this indictment. After we received an explanation, we will provide you with our opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, are you satisfied with the statement made by Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If not so, then please an explanation from your part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Very much so, Your Honours. There are a number of very notorious incidences that occur in this area, not only the illegal detention of Muslim people in the prison facility at Kaonik, which were taken out and used for the purposes of human shields and trench digging, which was notorious, uninvestigated and nothing was done about it, but there are other very notorious incidences that occurred and it's my purpose to show that nothing was done about them either. So that there's a consistent pattern of ignoring all of these atrocities that occurred in this area and that this witness was in a position to bring about or effect an investigation or at least inquire into it, but did nothing about it. That's my purpose, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann and Mr. Mikulicic, the Chamber determines that one should only ask the witness whether or not he had any relations with or any dealings with respect to these questions or these issues. Whether or not he knew -- I'm sorry, let me restate this. Whether or not there were any dealings and all other questions should be withdrawn. So there should be some facts that we can perhaps ask whether or not there was any type of trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any trial into --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any trial related to the perpetrators of the persons responsible for the truck bomb explosion in Stari Vitez that occurred on or about the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any trial in relation to the perpetrators who shelled the central downtown district of Zenica on the 19th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: If the request to open investigation was never submitted, then the judicial proceedings didn't take place. This is all provided for in the law on criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any investigation -- I'm sorry, any trial into the persons who were responsible for forcing Kaonik prisoners to go out and act as human shields or to dig trenches during the course of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: It was not conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any trial or investigation into an incident whereby convoys travelling through Vitez, on the 10th of June, 1993, were plundered, these humanitarian convoys plundered and the drivers killed, allegedly, by HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether such proceedings were conducted, because at that time I was in hospital undergoing a treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was any trial or investigation into the shooting by, allegedly by HVO soldiers, of an interpreter employed by the British battalion in Vitez in July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: This incident is completely unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The name of the victim was Dobrila Kalaba. Was there any trial in relation to the killing of civilian personnel, or civilians, in the Town of Ahmici in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, with all due respect, the Defence really cannot understand what kind of link these questions have with the role of the accused, Zlatko Aleksovski, in this particular trial. The accused, Zlatko Aleksovski, could in no way have influence on these proceedings or submission of criminal reports. This is why we simply don't understand what these questions have to do with the facts stated in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I am happy to respond to that. Mr. Aleksovski is part of the whole machinery that operated in this particular area of the Lasva Valley, especially in the period of 1993. This witness is being brought forward, presumably, to give evidence about one incident which was investigated and which he was involved in. I don't know what the Defence at the end of the day are going to do with this evidence, but it's my assumption that it's going to be presented as a basis upon which it could be argued that when incidences occurred, such as this particular one, action was taken by the superior of the prison, Mr. Aleksovski. Now, directly related to him is the taking of prisoners out of his facility and using them for the purposes for which they were used, which I have mentioned on numerous times, the subjecting them to inhumane conditions and beatings inside the prison, all of which are matters that he could have investigated, had investigated and pursued. And what I am showing, Your Honour, is that there is -- not only is it restricted or limited to what was happening in the camp itself, but it was a course of conduct that operated throughout the whole of the area. It's not suggested that Mr. Aleksovski is responsible for or any way meet as such directly with these atrocities, if I can call it that, in other parts of the municipality, but they are events which occurred in the area which is under the jurisdiction of this witness. And, Your Honours, it points to a pattern. So that what happened at Kaonik is not some mere coincidence, some aberration, but in fact constitutes an integral part of a plan and pattern of conduct which happened throughout the whole of Lasva Valley. Now, this witness had the jurisdiction to deal with criminal acts committed by members of the HVO. It is alleged that all of these incidences that I am mentioning were committed by members of the HVO, and would clearly have fallen under his jurisdiction should a report have been investigated. He may not have been responsible for the report, or commencing the investigation, but there are certainly matters which are notorious and well-known and at the time attracted international media coverage, and yet he seems, in most instances, not to have known anything about them. And yet nothing was done. So, Your Honours, my cross-examination goes to a number of points. It goes to that systematic conduct to show a wider scheme and pattern, which was operational. It also goes to the credibility of this witness. So there are the two foundations of my line of cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, what bothers me is this. You are putting to him facts which is alleged are notorious, and they are notorious to whom? Not to the Court. How do you put facts to him which are not proven?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can put matters to him, Your Honours, and he is in a position to state his reaction to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: But you are alleging facts, facts which are supposed to have happened and we know nothing about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the purpose of cross-examination is not only to confront the witness with matters which have been raised directly in chief, not only limited to matters which are part of the Prosecution's evidence, or the Defence evidence in the case, but it is permissible, in my respectful submission, to confront a witness with matters and for him to agree or deny them. And that's merely all I am doing, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Yes, but we are hearing the facts for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I have no control over the calling of the witness. The witness comes along for the first time now and tells us his responsibility. But I am prepared to put to the witness a document, if that would assist in providing a foundation, at least in relation to one of the incidences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Niemann. I would like to ask Mr. Mikulicic whether or not he has anything he wishes to add or whether he wishes to respond to the explanation given by Mr. Niemann in respect of your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. In his cross-examination Mr. Niemann starts from the assumption that in the area of the Lasva Valley some situations in excess of the ordinary happened, that that was the standard behaviour during that period of time. However, in this Tribunal and in this particular case, we do not have a model of conduct on trial, but proceedings are conducted against Mr. Aleksovski for certain spelled out acts. Mr. Aleksovski could in no way affect this model of conduct that the prosecutor refers to. Our second objection to this is that when examining the witness the Prosecution goes beyond the framework of the examination in chief. And, lastly, here we are not conducting the case against the witness. It is not the witness who is on trial. These are our objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In my opinion, the cross-examination should solely be placed within the scope of the examination in chief. Nonetheless, I think we are going to take advantage of this particular moment to take a break and then we will resume with the session. Thank you. Fifteen-minute recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: The issue has been decided by this Chamber in the following way: First, the cross-examination must be strictly within the scope of the examination in chief. Second, the Prosecution's questions dealing with the cases about which the witness may have been aware must be relevant to those charges made against the accused. This is the decision of the Chamber and I believe this is very clear. And so within these parameters, Mr. Niemann, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Niemann, could you please repeat what you just stated, your response, because the interpreters did not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, you have the floor. I would like to see whether you have any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Defence has no further questions for this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: When you were at the law school, did you receive courses on public international law and on humanitarian law in particular?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: As a military judge, had you jurisdiction on prisoners of war as defined by the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, I would also like to ask you a few questions. In your training in law, I believe you took law courses in Banja Luka, were you trained in general law, in constitutional law, as well as in administrative law?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Another thing. You stated that if you were to see something during your visits to Kaonik Prison, which was not going well with the prisoners, then you would submit such an issue to Mr. Aleksovski; is that correct? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes, if the matter related to detainees, they were the only ones under my jurisdiction, that is, persons against whom criminal proceedings were being conducted, until the -- until their sentencing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, you have jurisdiction solely over the prisoners of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Then you have nothing at all to do with the civilian prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Then to whom should Mr. Aleksovski address issues that you would have raised with him? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: If a detainee complained of the treatment received while in detention, then it was my duty to notify Mr. Aleksovski and at the same time notify the ministry in Mostar, that is the department for justice and the administration, which would then take further measures. It was all prescribed under and by law because we took over all the legislation of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the enforcement of laws and all the other by-laws, whatever concerned, the enforcement of these laws.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Aleksovski had some relationship with the Ministry of Justice; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Did he have any relations with the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it has to do -- what he had to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: To your knowledge, if someone wanted to visit the Kaonik Prison, would he have to request authorisation, and from whom?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Regarding the detainees, it was ordered from the court, that is either the presiding judge or the investigating judge. As I have said, in relation to the detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And if someone wanted to know how things were going in the prison, for example, if someone were coming from an international organisation?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they contacted Mr. Aleksovski directly. I wouldn't know the details. I don't know when they came, nor did I have any contact with international organisations, by this I mean the Red Cross in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Did the Busovaca police have anything to do with the Kaonik Prison?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Another thing I would like for you to clarify for me, if you can. How was the work organised within the prison? I am speaking now of the work of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I knew nothing about that. Convicted persons were under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice. In other words, these details about how work was organised there, I did not know that, nor was it my duty to know it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But if you go to the prison to see a prisoner, or a prisoner you wished to see, for example, in a particular case and he wasn't there, you would ask Mr. Aleksovski, and then Mr. Aleksovski would tell you he's out working. Would you then have anything to do with that situation or not?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I never heard such a case, because the detainees, persons in the custody, never went to work without ensuring the situation so they could escape. We have to understand that we were -- there was a state of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. So I believe, and at least the next question I wish to put to you, although it might be a bit redundant, but excuse me if I have to ask you anyway. What was the role of Mr. Aleksovski in the work of prisoners outside of the prison? Mr. Aleksovski was the director of the prison.

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, before the court he was the prison warden, and that is how we knew him, the commander of the district military prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But he was also the warden for the -- well, the director for the HVO, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: What do you mean director for HVO? It was the armoured component.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: My question is whether or not he was one hundred percent the director, or whether or not he was solely the director for the Ministry of Justice, but not for other areas. What would you say about that? If you can clarify that for me.

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I don't know what were the principles that governed the work, if he was the commander, as you say, 50/50 percent. I only know when his work had something to do with the court. And in that particular field his activity was quite regular, normal. And that is the only aspect that I can talk about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I understand that when I say 50 percent, that's a metaphor. So my question is if Mr. Aleksovski was the director of the prison or whether or not there were other persons who behind him were also managing and directing the prison. Do you have anything -- any knowledge about this?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Aleksovski was the warden of the district military prison, and I may also mention that there were three categories of persons who were members of the HVO. There were persons under custody and under the direct supervision of the court; two, there were convicts and they also fell -- they were under the Ministry of Justice; and three, there were people who had been punished for disciplinary measures and they were therefore sanctioned by the relevant commander of the relevant army formation for disciplinary transgressions. So there were three categories of persons who were in that prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But there were not three wardens, there was only one warden. So, in your opinion, was Mr. Aleksovski the warden of these three categories of persons?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. You stated that on several occasions you visited Kaonik Prison, you said March or April and July, for example. You certainly must have visited the prisoners who were within your jurisdiction, therefore, this was a certain category of prisoners. Did you see inter alia civilian prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I did not see civilian prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But you saw military prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: How were you distinguishing the military prisoners from the civilian prisoners in this prison? Did they have separate cells, were there some sort of external signs that you could see, that you noticed? How would you discern the two within the prison?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I paid a visit only to a wing of the prison which was separated, not physically, but they there were separate cells where persons were kept under custody, where persons were detained. I never entered any other rooms, nor did I have the need to enter them. And those were special rooms

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. I believe that the Chamber has no further questions to put to you. We thank you for having coming here to the International Criminal Tribunal and may wish you a pleasant return trip to your country. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With your permission, Mr. President, I like to recognise that with regards to document 134, the document of the Ahmici, 134, document 134.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to find out what we are going to do with such document, whether or not it's been admitted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, do you have any observations you would like to make with regards to the photograph of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, to begin with, I do not know whether my learned friend is tendering this photograph as evidence, or was it merely shown to the witness to remind him of certain events.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours it would go outside the scope of your ruling, so I wouldn't seek to tender it now, in view of Your Honours' decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. It is not admitted, then. And you no longer have need for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Will the court usher please escort the witness out. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I see then today our work is done, but we shall find ourselves again in this room on the 29th of June for the continuation and for the week. I believe this is in our scheduled sessions, the 29th, the 30th, the 1st of July, and up to the 3rd of July, I believe. Is that not right? All right. Until then, continue with your work and I will see you all. Thank you to the technicians and to the interpreters.
